concepts.name: Creative media
concepts.definition: Creation or production of audio, video, images, or other media.

concepts.name: Communication and collaboration
concepts.definition: Interpersonal communication or coordinated group work.

concepts.name: Knowledge and productivity
concepts.definition: Knowledge capture, organization, and personal or team productivity.

concepts.name: Software development
concepts.definition: Design, implementation, testing, or maintenance of software.

concepts.name: Data and analytics
concepts.definition: Data processing, analysis, or visualization.

concepts.name: Networking and distributed systems
concepts.definition: Network communication or coordination among distributed nodes.

concepts.name: Security and privacy
concepts.definition: Protection of systems, communications, identities, or data.

concepts.name: Storage, sync, and backup
concepts.definition: Durable storage, replication, synchronization, or backup.

concepts.name: Infrastructure and operations
concepts.definition: Deployment, operation, or observation of computing infrastructure.

concepts.name: Web content and publishing
concepts.definition: Creation, management, or publication of web content.

concepts.name: Science and engineering
concepts.definition: Scientific research, simulation, measurement, or engineering work.

concepts.name: Audio workstation
concepts.definition: A tool for recording, editing, arranging, or mixing multitrack audio.

concepts.name: Audio plug-in host
concepts.definition: A tool capable of loading audio plug-ins for processing or instruments.

concepts.name: Messenger
concepts.definition: A tool whose primary role is person-to-person or group messaging.

concepts.name: File synchronization tool
concepts.definition: A tool that synchronizes files across locations or devices.

concepts.name: Networking protocol or stack
concepts.definition: A protocol or implementation stack for networked communication.

concepts.name: Distributed collaboration framework
concepts.definition: A developer framework for collaborative or replicated applications.

concepts.name: Database
concepts.definition: A system whose primary role is storing and querying structured data.

concepts.name: Developer framework
concepts.definition: A reusable framework for building software.

concepts.name: Self-hosted application
concepts.definition: An end-user application intended to run on user-controlled infrastructure.

concepts.name: Knowledge application
concepts.definition: An end-user tool for capturing or organizing knowledge.

concepts.name: End-to-end encryption
concepts.definition: Provides documented content encryption in which service intermediaries cannot access plaintext within the stated threat model.

concepts.name: Peer-to-peer synchronization or exchange
concepts.definition: Synchronizes or exchanges application data directly among peer nodes rather than requiring one canonical data server.

concepts.name: Pluggable transports
concepts.definition: Allows an operator or integrator to select or add transport implementations through a documented interface.

concepts.name: Self-hostable
concepts.definition: Can be deployed and operated on infrastructure controlled by the user or organization.

concepts.name: Open-source status
concepts.definition: Source is available under a license meeting an explicitly stated open-source criterion; fixture uses OSI-approved or equivalent project-stated licensing.

concepts.name: Linux support
concepts.definition: Provides a documented supported Linux runtime or desktop build.

concepts.name: Transport used
concepts.definition: A named transport or bearer used by the tool in the described configuration.

concepts.name: Primary deployment mode
concepts.definition: The primary documented operating arrangement for the tool.

concepts.name: VST3 host support
concepts.definition: Degree to which an audio plug-in host can load and operate VST3 plug-ins.

concepts.name: LV2 host support
concepts.definition: Degree to which an audio plug-in host can load and operate LV2 plug-ins.

concepts.name: WebDAV support
concepts.definition: Interoperates with WebDAV for remote file or content access.

concepts.name: Transport agnosticism
concepts.definition: Rubric-based magnitude of how independently the system model and APIs operate from any one network transport.

anchors.0: Hard-wired to one transport with transport assumptions in the data model.
anchors.5: Some transport substitution is possible but core workflows or identity retain transport coupling.
anchors.8: Multiple materially different transports are documented behind stable abstractions.
anchors.10: Transport-independent model with demonstrated third-party transport extension and no privileged bearer.

concepts.name: Synchronization decentralization
concepts.definition: Rubric-based magnitude of independence from a mandatory coordinating service for normal synchronization.

anchors.0: A vendor-controlled central service is mandatory.
anchors.5: Self-hosting or federation is possible but coordination remains server-centric.
anchors.8: Normal operation can proceed directly among peers without a mandatory shared service.
anchors.10: No privileged coordinator is required for discovery, authorization, or data exchange.

concepts.name: Local-first
concepts.definition: Informal discovery label indicating that local operation and local data ownership are emphasized.

concepts.name: Modular
concepts.definition: Informal discovery label indicating an architecture designed around replaceable components.

unresolved.note: The fixture uses project licensing evidence, but organizational policy should define the acceptance criterion before hard selection.
Full currently means project-documented hosting, not conformance testing across every extension.
Pluggability is a deterministic advertised capability; agnosticism is a rubric assessment of coupling magnitude.
